order: Fix a critical finding in the abandoned-worktree sweep. Its prefix guard currently classifies any worktree path merely containing the checkout prefix as a leftover and removes its parent directory outright; on macOS and Windows continuous-integration runners that parent turns out to be the operating system's own temporary root when the fixture repository's own temp-directory name happens to match, and the same class reproduces independently for a legitimate worktree nested under a prefix-matching ancestor directory. Replace the substring classification with a structural check: identification must match exactly the tmp-root, prefix, and checkout shape, not a mere substring; skip the main worktree outright in every case; and remove only the literal prefix-named parent — no broader deletion is ever performed. Pin both reproducer shapes as regressions. Record the review verdict verbatim in the roster, and keep the tranche marked open pending the next review pass.
claims: Identification of abandoned worktrees is now structural rather than substring-based: the main worktree is skipped outright, and only the prefix-named parent directory is ever removed. Both reproducer shapes — the operating-system temp-root collision and the legitimate nested worktree — are pinned as regressions. The review verdict was recorded verbatim. Verifier tallied 96, router 135, and registry 31, each suite finishing with zero failures on the local pass, while the tranche stays held at REVISE pending the next review.
